For Los Angeles (LA) grades C and D reflux oesophagitis, the optimal time for acid suppression therapy to achieve maximal healing has been a subject of interest. According to various studies and matches from our local dataset, the current consensus is that 4 weeks' acid-suppressive therapy is sufficient to induce significant healing in both LA C and D oesophagitis.

These studies suggest that after initiating acid suppressive therapy for 4 weeks, patients typically achieve a substantial reduction in acid reflux symptoms, which correlates with improved quality of life. While the duration of treatment may vary depending on individual patient responses and factors such as medication adherence, it appears that 4 weeks is a generally optimal time frame for maximal healing.

It's essential to note that early initiation of therapy is beneficial, but once established, further treatment may not be necessary unless symptoms persist or recur. The fact that patients can achieve significant healing without preoperative fasting also indicates that it is not strictly necessary in all cases.

In summary, based on the available data and matches from our local dataset, 4 weeks' acid-suppressive therapy appears to be an optimal time frame for maximal healing of LA C and D reflux oesophagitis.
